DC-2025-B260798.title: Health-Care Decisions Amendment Act of 2026

actions.text: Public Hearing on B26-0798
Notice of Public Hearing filed in the Office of Secretary by Health
Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0798 Published in the District of Columbia Register
Referred to Committee on Health
B26-0798 Introduced by Chairman Mendelson at Office of the Secretary

documents.label: Notice of Public Hearing filed in the Office of Secretary by Health

DC-2025-B260798.aiSummary: The bill would change District rules for MOST forms, which are medical forms that record a patient’s treatment wishes. It would let more health workers help prepare and sign these forms, including advanced practice nurses, naturopathic physicians, and physician assistants under delegation agreements, and it would update the MOST Advisory Committee. It would also require completed MOST forms to be put in the patient’s electronic medical record and kept as part of the permanent record until revoked.

DC-2025-B260839.aiSummary: The bill would symbolically name 50th Street NE, between East Capitol Street NE and Ames Street NE in Ward 7, as "Johnny Gant Way." It is meant to honor Johnny Gant, a longtime Ward 7 resident, boxer, businessman, coach, and mentor. The change would take effect after mayoral approval and a 30-day congressional review period.

DC-2025-B260875.title: Parking and Traffic Ticket Penalty Reduction Amendment Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to Committee on Transportation and the Environment
Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0875 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0875 Introduced by Councilmember T. White at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260875.aiSummary: The measure would change how District parking and traffic tickets are handled, including tickets from automated traffic cameras and some parking, standing, stopping, and pedestrian offenses. It would remove one added penalty for not answering some notices within 30 days, and it would set a 60-day answer period for notices of infraction in another part of the law. People with these tickets, and some vehicle lessors, would be affected.

DC-2025-B260361.aiSummary: The bill would phase out sales and distribution of mercury-containing compact fluorescent and linear fluorescent lamps in the District, with some narrow exceptions for things like medical, research, and special-use lamps. It would affect retailers and distributors, and the Department of Energy and the Environment would inspect stores, track complaints, and issue warnings or fines for violations. The limits would start on July 1, 2027 for some compact fluorescent lamps and on July 1, 2028 for other compact fluorescent lamps and linear fluorescent lamps.

DC-2025-B260820.aiSummary: The bill would require the Mayor to send the Office of Tax and Revenue a list of District properties with affordability rules, including affordable housing and inclusionary zoning. It is meant to help property tax assessments reflect the lower rent limits on those homes. It affects owners of affordable housing and other properties with District-imposed affordability limits.
